sections.title: One known form, now a whole pattern
sections.content: Back in A1 you learned menj ("go!") as one fixed, irregular form. Now you get the general pattern behind it: to tell someone to do something, add -j to the verb's stem. vág ("to cut"), kever ("to stir, mix") and forral ("to boil") are all regular stems, so the -j attaches directly, with nothing in between.

Not every verb takes a plain -j — some stems change shape when "j" lands on them, the same way you'll see next lesson. vág, kever and forral are the three "easy" ones to start with, exactly as written here, no changes.
